title: The Morning Build for July 17, 2026: Open-weights from Moonshot, Capital One Open-Sources VulnHunter, and Apple Sues OpenAI
intro: Today’s thread ties model-weight openness, enterprise security tooling, and legal risk: Moonshot and Kimi pushed large open-weight models into public release windows while Capital One published an Apache 2.0 AI-driven vulnerability scanner on GitHub, and Apple filed a trade-secrets suit that could affect OpenAI’s hardware and IPO timeline.
meta_description: Moonshot’s Kimi K3 nears 3T params and full weights by July 27; Capital One open-sources VulnHunter under Apache 2.0; Apple sues OpenAI, risking the company’s IPO timeline.

stories.headline: Capital One open-sources VulnHunter under Apache 2.0, an attacker-first, falsifying AI vulnerability scanner
stories.what_happened: Capital One published VulnHunter on GitHub under an Apache 2.0 license; the tool uses an attacker-first forward analysis, a falsification engine that tries to disprove findings, and generates targeted patch proposals, and currently runs on Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 inside a Claude Code environment.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers get an enterprise-grade, agentic open-source scanner that traces exploit paths forward from external entry points, reduces false positives via automated falsification, and outputs context-aware remediation suggestions rather than generic advisories.
stories.outlook: Public activity on the GitHub repository, forks, issues, pull requests, and community stress tests, will be the next concrete signal of adoption and third-party validation of VulnHunter’s attacker-first and falsification features.

stories.headline: Apple sues OpenAI for trade-secret misappropriation while OpenAI eyes an IPO later this year
stories.what_happened: Apple filed a trade-secrets lawsuit against OpenAI alleging misconduct that includes hiring more than 400 former Apple employees and implicates senior OpenAI hardware staff; OpenAI has issued a guarded response and the dispute arrives as the company reportedly considers an IPO later this year.
stories.why_it_matters: Legal claims aimed at hardware and personnel could constrain OpenAI’s hardware roadmap, raise due-diligence burdens for partners, and introduce regulatory and IP risk into any near-term public offering or large procurement that depends on clarifying those allegations.
stories.outlook: OpenAI’s IPO timeline, reported as possible later this year, is the next major milestone to watch because court developments and discovery could affect the offering window and disclosure requirements.

stories.headline: Moonshot’s Kimi K3 is expected to be a 2–3 trillion-parameter open-weight model released in the coming days
stories.what_happened: Reports cite anonymous sources saying Moonshot AI’s upcoming Kimi K3 will have between 2 trillion and 3 trillion parameters and is expected to be released in the coming days, positioning it as China’s largest open-weight model and aiming to close the gap with Anthropic’s Opus 4.8.
stories.why_it_matters: A multi-trillion-parameter open-weight release changes engineering trade-offs for regulated and on-premise deployments by making a high-capability model available outside closed-cloud APIs, and it sharpens questions about export-control efficacy and compute sourcing.
stories.outlook: The reported imminent release is the next concrete milestone; the initial public availability window in the coming days will show what parts of K3 (API access, hosted serving, or weights) Moonshot opens first.

stories.headline: Early assessments say Kimi K3 matches Opus 4.8 on many tasks but demands large-memory GPUs and narrows cost gaps
stories.what_happened: Coverage and analysis report Kimi K3 at roughly 2.8 trillion parameters using a mixture-of-experts setup that does not fit on a single Nvidia DGX B200 even with FP4 quantization, requiring higher-memory systems like GB300 NVL72 or B300; early impressions rate K3 close to Opus 4.8 with higher token costs than prior Chinese open models.
stories.why_it_matters: Engineers planning to run or host K3 must target multi-hundred-GB GPU memory servers or specialized accelerators, and the model’s higher inference cost reduces the previous operational price advantage of Chinese open models for long-context, agentic workflows.
stories.outlook: Independent benchmark releases and cost-per-task analyses from labs such as Artificial Analysis will be the next public checks on K3’s claimed parity and operational cost profile.

stories.headline: Kimi publishes K3 technical details: 2.8T params, 1M-token context, mixture-of-experts, and full weights due by July 27
stories.what_happened: Kimi’s release notes and reporting state K3 uses 2.8 trillion parameters, a mixture-of-experts architecture with 896 experts (16 active per token), a one-million-token context window, multimodal input, and that full model weights are scheduled for release by July 27; K3 is already available via Kimi.com, mobile apps, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and listed on OpenRouter under moonshotai/kimi-k3.
stories.why_it_matters: The technical specs matter for deployment: 1M-token contexts and MoE sparsity change memory and serving designs, and the July 27 weights release date gives engineering teams a concrete timeline to plan on-premise evaluation, memory provisioning, and integration testing.
stories.outlook: July 27 is the explicit milestone for full weight publication; that date will let teams confirm memory-footprint claims, validate the million-token context behavior, and begin self-hosted experiments.

narration_script: Capital One published VulnHunter as an open-source, Apache 2.0 project that reasons forward from attacker entry points, runs a built-in falsification workflow to drop false positives, and generates targeted patch proposals. The tool is currently orchestrated on Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.8 inside Claude Code. The next concrete signal for engineers will be public activity on the GitHub repository, forks, issues, pull requests, and community stress tests that validate the attacker-first and falsification features. Apple has filed a trade-secrets lawsuit against OpenAI, alleging misconduct that touches senior hardware staff and more than 400 former Apple employees now at OpenAI. OpenAI has given a careful response, and the timing intersects a reported IPO timeline later this year, making the offering window the next major milestone to watch because litigation and discovery could affect the process. Reports say Moonshot AI will release Kimi K3 in the coming days as China’s largest open-weight model, with sources placing it between 2 trillion and 3 trillion parameters and positioning it to close the gap with Anthropic’s Opus 4.8. Early coverage and hardware analysis note that K3’s scale requires GPUs with hundreds of gigabytes of memory and that the model narrows cost differences with Western mid-range models. Independent benchmark publications and cost-per-task analyses from labs like Artificial Analysis are the next public checks on K3’s performance claims. Kimi’s own technical briefings list K3 at 2.8 trillion parameters with a mixture-of-experts architecture activating 16 of 896 experts, a one-million-token context window, multimodal input, and claims of faster decoding via a Kimi Delta Attention change. Kimi says the full model weights will be published by July 27 and the model is already available through Kimi.com, mobile apps, Kimi Work, Kimi Code, and OpenRouter under moonshotai/kimi-k3. That July 27 weights date is the concrete milestone engineers can use to schedule on-premise evaluations, confirm memory and context behavior, and begin self-hosted tests.
